followup_explanation:
This was a friendly, technical math question with no harm-adjacent content, so the safety/aversion dimensions that differentiate these models don't apply here. That makes it a straightforward capability decision.

Dunlin-235B outperforms Avocet-235B across the relevant benchmarks — notably MMLU-Pro (81.2 vs 75.4), GPQA Diamond (64.1 vs 55.6), and IFEval (89.8 vs 86.2). The higher reasoning and instruction-following scores matter for a quantitative problem that requires both correct binomial computation and precise adherence to the formatting instruction ("round to the nearest thousandth").

The task preferences didn't tip the decision: the query is warm and benign, so Avocet's aversion effects wouldn't penalize it, and it's not especially open-ended/generative, so Avocet's preference for novel creative work doesn't strongly favor it either. With preferences roughly neutral, raw capability is the deciding factor, and Dunlin is the stronger choice.
